title: Pitch story for considered purchases
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether the business needs a pitch story, and how to build it from positioning: insight, alternatives as approaches, the agreed ideal, differentiated value, proof, objections, one ask.
applies_when: Considered purchase where buyers compare approaches
required_inputs: The champion's shortlist and alternatives (including do nothing)
evidence_requirements: number of people in the decision
documented five positioning components with evidence
who sits in the first call (champion)
industry research only if the insight needs backing
who uses the product vs who buys it
who owns the problem at target accounts
unit cost of the problem (owner or customer inputs)
proof in the buyer's own metrics
missing_data_behavior: Unproven position: pitch is a thesis; review when positioning changes.

decision_branches.then: Tailored demo; otherwise lead with strongest differentiators.
Reuse on homepage, buyer's guide and onboarding.

implementation_steps: Read salesMotion, salesCycle, aov, complexity and customerType
Record the reason so the owner can override
Check each component exists with evidence
Map: insight <- value + best-fit; alternatives <- alternatives; perfect world <- value; introduction <- category; value step <- value + capabilities; proof <- proof
Take objections and ask from sales history
Write one insight from value + best-fit (one slide, 1-2 minutes)
Group alternatives into 2-5 approaches incl. status quo
For each: pros and cons for this buyer type (few words)
Pick the pitch parts it needs
Keep all assets on one pitch/positioning version
State the problem so a peer would say 'yes, and...'
Name the role that owns it at different company sizes
Calculate the cost of the problem in code from inputs (hard vs soft)
dependencies: a sales conversation exists (call, demo, consult, site visit) or a long-form page/video the buyer studies
positioning canvas from the positioning skill / 03_positioning.md workflow

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: owner or rep time for calls
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: someone who can hold a guided conversation

metrics: share of sales conversations ending with an agreed next step
share of deals where pitched alternatives matched the real shortlist
share of calls where perfect-world criteria were agreed
share of disagreements that were bad-fit on review
activation to first value for product-led onboarding
share of meetings where the prospect confirms the problem
guardrails: The insight is what buyers misunderstand, not 'what changed' or a trend.
Vision stories suit investors; buyers get a reason to act now, not to wait.
The gate is a strategic preference, not a hard block; owner can override
No pitch claim without a positioning component behind it
Every claim about an alternative needs evidence (review, doc, demo, owner-verified)
No invented research to back the insight
Buyer's guide comparisons follow the same evidence rule as the pitch
Marketing consent for guide leads before nurture
Every number comes from confirmed facts or a deterministic calculation
alternatives_when_constrained: No sales conversation at all: carry insight + value themes into the page or a buyer's guide (K7)
No customers yet: thesis positioning plus broad exposure (BK03 exploration mode)
No live calls: put insight + approaches on a long-form page or buyer's guide (K7)
No video budget: long-form page section with the same order
No sales team: the buyer's guide and page do the teaching
No customer evidence: label themes as hypotheses and run PB-interviews
stop_conditions: Revisit when price, sales motion or buyer group changes
Positioning review triggers (new shortlisted competitor, capability change, buyer change) also invalidate the pitch version
Prospects repeatedly don't recognise their situation in the approaches: rewrite alternatives
Many good-fit prospects disagree at perfect world: positioning problem, go back to K2
Positioning version change invalidates all derived assets
If most prospects reject the problem framing, go back to positioning and VoC, not more outreach
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Applying B2B storyboard to a $15 consumer product adds friction
Treating a high-stakes consumer purchase as unconsidered (toilet case shows guidance helps)
Pitch built from features because positioning was skipped
Pitching to the economic buyer in call one when the champion screens vendors
Trend-as-insight ('more data than ever', 'AI adoption is accelerating')
Pasting the 8 slides onto the homepage
Buyer's guide that just lists your features
A trend made up to create urgency

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: generate a pitch storyboard only when salesMotion is sales_assisted or sales_led, or salesCycle is medium/long, or aov is high; otherwise skip and say why
proposed: cap value themes at three in pitch and messaging outputs
proposed: flag an insight that would read the same for the top competitor (swap test) or matches a generic-trend pattern
proposed: target setup at or under about a fifth of first-call time; warn above
proposed: add 'buyer's guide' as a lead-magnet type for considered B2B purchases, built from insight + approaches
proposed: the positioning pitch narrative includes a cost-of-problem line computed in code from owner or customer inputs, labelled hard or soft.
proposed: tag each competitive alternative as none, process, service provider or product; a prospect already paying a provider or product counts as a nice-to-have fit signal in prospecting.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: for local services, use the compressed 'teach how to choose' form only for high-ticket considered jobs
proposed: perfect-world criteria must each map to a value theme; unmapped criteria are dropped
proposed: homepage briefs use category + up to 3 value themes + proof; full storyboard order only for long-form pages, explainers and buyer's guides
proposed: 'what has changed' stays optional and is cut when no real, observable change exists (keep positioning step 8).

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: a pitch artifact must reference a PositioningVersion id; if that version changes, the pitch is marked stale

external_requirement.rule: proposed: claims about a named competitor's limits require cited evidence, as for any comparative claim

reconciliation_note: Versions Obviously Awesome guidance; new material is the storyboard and the applicability gate.
